recentItems.title: RUSSIA UNLEASHES HELL! Kyiv Rocked by Missile Strikes as Explosions Shake Capital | ET Now
recentItems.description:
Russian missiles struck Kyiv in three waves overnight on October 19, killing at least one person and injuring eight, according to Ukrainian officials and reporting by the Kyiv Independent. The strikes damaged residential buildings, a medical facility, a shopping centre and metro infrastructure across at least three districts, prompting temporary closures at two above-ground metro stations. Questions have also emerged over the timing of air-raid warnings, with journalists reporting that sirens sounded as explosions were already unfolding. The attack comes amid renewed attention to US intelligence-sharing with Ukraine and growing concerns over Russia’s reported campaign against Ukrainian energy infrastructure ahead of winter. A separate report alleging plans to target key energy facilities has not been independently verified. The latest barrage underscores the continuing threat to civilians and critical infrastructure as Russia’s war against Ukraine continues.

recentItems.title: CHAOS IN MILAN! Streets Tense as Rioters Target Shops and Police Move In | ET Now | World News
recentItems.description:
Milan was left with smashed shop windows, damaged vehicles and vandalised businesses on Sunday, October 18, after a cost-of-living demonstration descended into clashes between protesters and police the previous day. Footage from central Milan showed shattered glass across streets, overturned furniture, a ransacked supermarket and officers patrolling near the city's cathedral. At least 25 people, including around 10 police officers, were reportedly injured and taken to hospital, although none of the injuries was considered serious. The demonstration began peacefully before protesters allegedly threw stones and other objects at police, while shops were vandalised and barricades set alight. Officers responded with tear gas and water cannon. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni condemned the violence, while Milan Mayor Giuseppe Sala acknowledged protesters' concerns but said attacks on police and destruction of property were unjustifiable. The clashes highlight growing public discontent over living costs in Italy amid a wider wave of protests across Europe.

recentItems.title: ZELENSKY LEFT OUT? Putin Floats Trump-Xi Talks to Decide Ukraine’s Future | ET Now | World News
recentItems.description:
Russian President Vladimir Putin has proposed a summit with US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping to discuss a possible end to the Ukraine war, potentially without Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky at the table, The Wall Street Journal reported. Moscow has suggested holding the talks on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China, on November 18–19. The proposal comes amid closer engagement between Trump and Putin, including a reported Russian diesel deal and a US waiver of key sanctions on Moscow. However, a senior US official told the Journal that Trump has not agreed to the meeting, while Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed that discussions over a potential summit were taking place. The proposed format raises questions about Ukraine’s role in peace negotiations, China’s ambitions as a diplomatic power broker and the potential sidelining of European governments.
